title: Cluster provisioning probe notes
content:
Context / symptom:
- New autoscaling pool (pool-a) provisioned via terraform + helm chart 'nodepool-bootstrap' keeps failing to reach Ready state intermittently (~1-2 nodes per deploy).
- Nodes show as NotReady for a few minutes then become Ready. Sometimes they never join and get GC'd by the autoscaler.
- Problem started after we bumped image to ubuntu-24 + containerd 1.8 in the machine image.

Observations so far:
- kubelet logs often show: "failed to get node info: error determining node address" for ~30-90s during boot.
- When NotReady, 'kubectl describe node <node>' shows kubelet conditions: NetworkUnavailable True, KubeletReady False, MemoryPressure False.
- journalctl -u kubelet on affected node contains repeated: "Failed to start Container runtime: failed to connect to container runtime: dial unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connect: no such file or directory" for a while, then resolves when containerd comes up.
- There are occasional systemd cgroup warnings in kubelet: "cgroup v2 is not fully supported" — kernel/config mismatch maybe.
- iptables rules are missing early on; ip forwarding sysctl sometimes 0 on boot (sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0) which breaks CNI init timing.
- GCE-specific: DHCP lease sometimes delayed (metadata service slow) — seen on 2 nodes out of 50.

Commands I ran (timestamps local):
- ssh into node: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager\  <-- looked for start-up errors
  snippet: "level=error msg=\"Failed to start Container runtime: failed to connect to container runtime: dial unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connect: no such file or directory\""
- sudo systemctl status containerd.service\  --> On failing nodes: containerd crashed earlier; restart succeeded later.
- sudo crictl ps -a  (when socket up) -> shows kube-apiserver pods pending on node init (pause containers missing)
- cat /proc/cmdline -> checked cgroup flags (systemd vs cgroupfs) - kernel boot uses cgroup_no_v1=... nothing obvious
- sudo sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables -> 0 on boot; we set to 1 manually and applied CNI restart -> node transitions to Ready faster.
- sudo modprobe br_netfilter -> fixed bridge-nf module loaded; but module sometimes not present until later in boot.
- sudo journalctl -b | grep -E "br_netfilter|bridge-nf|docker|containerd|kubelet"  (collect timeline per boot)

Helm / infra artifacts examined:
- Helm chart: infra/nodepool-bootstrap values: postStart script runs a systemd unit to ensure br_netfilter and sysctl are set; but if cloud-init delays or systemd ordering wrong, kubelet starts before the postStart runs.
- Chart has pre-upgrade hook that writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-bridge.conf. Might race with cloud-init.
- There's a startup systemd unit 'ensure-provision.service' that runs before kubelet via Wants=, but Not always; unit has ConditionPathExists=/etc/provision-ready which sometimes isn't created due to cloud-init error.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between node boot sequence (cloud-init) and kubelet startup: kubelet starts before containerd or network/sysctl are configured -> kubelet transiently fails to register and autoscaler marks unhealthy.
2) containerd service occasionally crashes on first boot (due to outdated config or overlay/aufs issues with ubuntu-24 image) -> socket missing leads to kubelet errors.
3) cgroup v2/cgroup driver mismatch between containerd and kubelet causing intermittent errors and kubelet logs show warnings that delay readiness check.
4) Cloud DHCP/metadata slowness causing kubelet to be unable to determine node address for short window (metdata timeouts).

Quick repro attempt plan:
- Create a small pool (3 nodes) with identical image and add a deliberately slowed cloud-init (sleep 60 in cloud-init to simulate delay). Observe ordering.
- Add debug cloud-init that writes timestamps for each step to /var/log/provision-timeline.log (cloud-init-start, containerd-start, br_netfilter-load, kubelet-start).

Workarounds tested (and results):
- Delay kubelet via systemd: added ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 30 in kubelet.service -> fewer failures in canary cluster (2/30 fail -> 0/30). Not ideal (hack).
- Set postStart to run earlier (WantedBy=multi-user.target) / ensure-provision.service Before=kubelet.service -> reduced races but still occasional glitch.
- Added a systemd tmpfile to ensure /run/containerd exists earlier -> didn't help when containerd itself crashed.
- Explicitly enable br_netfilter via cloud-init early -> seems to fix the iptables issue on 100% of repros. Suggests ordering problem is real.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Rebuild machine image with containerd config validated against cgroup v2 (bake image with the exact containerd version we run in prod).
- Update helm chart to: 1) make ensure-provision.service RequiredBy=kubelet.service (hard dependency) 2) convert postStart script to cloud-init snippet (so lower-level) 3) emit provisioning timeline logs for future debugging.
- Add transient retry logic to autoscaler health probe for first 5 minutes (reduce aggressive GC of new nodes).
- Create a short runbook: what to check when new nodes are NotReady (commands below).

Runbook notes (commands to check on an affected node):
- journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo systemctl status containerd.service --no-pager
- sudo ls -l /run/containerd/containerd.sock || echo 'socket missing'
- sudo sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables; sudo modprobe br_netfilter; sudo cat /etc/sysctl.d/99-bridge.conf
- kubectl describe node <node> --show-events
- kubectl get cs; kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces | grep <node>
- ssh and grep /var/log/cloud-init-output.log and /var/log/provision-timeline.log (if present)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If we can't fully control cloud-init timing across regions, better to move these sysctl/module steps into the image bootstrap (baked in) rather than runtime hooks.
- We should add a small readiness gate in the autoscaler: allow 3 mins for kubelet to register before marking as unhealthy. Could be config in cluster-autoscaler.
- Watch for containerd segfaults in dmesg (possible kernel/overlayfs incompatibility).

Log excerpts (redacted ids):
- kubelet: "E0214 07:12:33.112345  1234 kubelet_node_status.go:70] Error updating node status, will retry: failed to get node info: error determining node address"
- containerd: "time=\"2025-02-14T07:11:58Z\" level=error msg=\"failed to start containerd: listen unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: bind: permission denied\"" (interesting - could be SELinux? but ubuntu default doesn't enforce)

Slack threads / context links:
- #infra-provisioning: thread tldr -> initial regression seen after image bump to ubuntu-24 (link pinned)
- See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-provisioning/pull/128 for the helm changes we rolled out (postStart, systemd unit).

If I forget later (short checklist):
1) Is containerd socket present? 2) br_netfilter loaded and sysctl applied? 3) cloud-init finished? 4) any containerd segfaults in dmesg? 5) kubelet cgroup driver matches containerd?

End of scratchpad.

--Marcus
